hook: The emperor under whom Japan went from samurai to steamships in one lifetime.

pages.x: Mutsuhito was born in Kyoto in 1852. For centuries the emperors had lived shut away in Kyoto, while the shoguns ruled. The year after his birth, American warships arrived and forced Japan to open its ports to trade.
He became emperor at 14. In 1868 rebels overthrew the last shogun and gave power back to the emperor. His reign was named Meiji, "enlightened rule", and he became known by it.
He moved from Kyoto to the shogun's city of Edo, renamed Tokyo, the eastern capital, and lived in the shogun's old castle. It is still the imperial palace.

Japan abolished the samurai class and the old feudal lords, built railways, telegraphs and factories, opened schools for every child, and created a modern army and navy. In a single generation it became an industrial power.
He cut his topknot, grew a beard, wore Western uniforms and ate beef, to show his people new ways. He hated being photographed, so his official portrait was a photograph of a drawing.
In 1889 he gave Japan a constitution and an elected parliament, the first in East Asia, modelled partly on Germany's.

Japan defeated China in 1895 and took Taiwan. In 1905 it shocked the world by beating Russia, the first time in modern history an Asian country had defeated a European great power. In 1910 it took over Korea.
He wrote around 100,000 short poems, called waka, in his lifetime.

He died in 1912. On the day of his funeral, General Nogi, a hero of the war with Russia, and his wife took their own lives to follow their emperor, in the old samurai way. The Meiji Shrine in Tokyo honours him.
In his 45-year reign Japan went from an isolated land of samurai to a modern industrial nation and empire, the first outside the West to do so.
pts: Japan modernised in a single generation
